entries.description: Monthly serial. Accurate immunology carried by an ensemble workplace comedy. The cells of the human body personified as workers in a vast facility,…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Accurate immunology carried by an ensemble workplace comedy. The cells of the human body personified as workers in a vast facility, in a serial that teaches immunology correctly while running as a comedy, and which reached far outside the educational market. The discipline that makes it work is that each character's behaviour is constrained by what the cell actually does, so the story cannot drift from the science without breaking the cast — `trope-55`'s group-with-a-job, with the job supplying the constraint. It is the clearest modern evidence that a commission and an audience are not opposed.

entries.category: The Prewar and Early Postwar Shōjo Line
entries.name: 謎のクローバー / Nazo no Clover
entries.author: Matsumoto Katsuji
entries.awards: None; the prize system postdates it by decades.
entries.description: One-shot. An early modern shōjo page, cited for a cinematic panel sense that the standard account places forty years later. The card exists to date…
entries.text: One-shot. An early modern shōjo page, cited for a cinematic panel sense that the standard account places forty years later. The card exists to date a formal claim rather than to recommend the work: if a 1934 girls'-magazine strip is already cutting between distances and staging a figure across panels, then `history-13`'s contested invention narrative has a prewar problem. The original prints 謎 as a question mark, which the roster holds because a title that cannot be typed is a title that generates variants.

entries.category: The Prewar and Early Postwar Shōjo Line
entries.name: くるくるクルミちゃん / Kurukuru Kurumi-chan
entries.author: Matsumoto Katsuji
entries.description: Monthly serial. A girls'-magazine strip that ran across roughly thirty-five years and several titles, interrupted by the war and resumed after it —…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A girls'-magazine strip that ran across roughly thirty-five years and several titles, interrupted by the war and resumed after it — one of the few continuous threads across the break `history-12` describes. Its protagonist is a modern, stylish girl rather than a moral lesson, which was the prewar shōjo page's actual innovation and is what the 1970s generation inherited before rebuilding it.

entries.category: The Prewar and Early Postwar Shōjo Line
entries.name: あんみつ姫 / Anmitsu Hime
entries.author: Kurakane Shōsuke
entries.description: Monthly serial. A postwar girls' serial that ran to 1955 across magazine, radio, film and stage — an early and complete media-mix, decades before…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A postwar girls' serial that ran to 1955 across magazine, radio, film and stage — an early and complete media-mix, decades before the term. `craft-30`'s distinction between the property and the story is visible here in its first commercial form: the character travelled, the serial did not have to.

entries.category: The Prewar and Early Postwar Shōjo Line
entries.name: リボンの騎士 / Ribon no Kishi
entries.author: Tezuka Osamu
entries.description: Monthly serial. A princess raised as a prince, in the shōjo magazine that most later accounts treat as the modern category's origin. Two cautions…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A princess raised as a prince, in the shōjo magazine that most later accounts treat as the modern category's origin. Two cautions the roster holds. The English market knows it as *Princess Knight*, and **three distinct versions exist** — the 1953 run carded here, and two later rewrites — so a citation without a date is a citation to nothing in particular. `author-28` is the standing counter-example to reading this as the transformation's start.

entries.category: The Prewar and Early Postwar Shōjo Line
entries.name: 魔法使いサリー / Sally the Witch
entries.author: Yokoyama Mitsuteru
entries.description: Monthly serial. The serial that founded the magical-girl line, by a creator better known for the giant robot — a range `author-65` cards. **The…
entries.text: Monthly serial. The serial that founded the magical-girl line, by a creator better known for the giant robot — a range `author-65` cards. **The title changed after publication began**: five instalments ran as 魔法使いサニー before a trademark conflict forced the retitle, so the original title differs from every catalogue entry. That is a phantom-duplicate generator of the purest kind, and `checklist-15` exists for it.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: アラベスク / Arabesuku
entries.author: Yamagishi Ryōko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A ballet serial by a creator trained in ballet, and the earliest of her works to show what the 1970s generation was about to do with…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A ballet serial by a creator trained in ballet, and the earliest of her works to show what the 1970s generation was about to do with the page: posture and gesture carrying emotional information that the dialogue never states. The creator's given name generates Ryōko, Ryoko and Ryouko across the record; the pack holds the macron form, per `checklist-15`.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: ポーの一族 / Pō no Ichizoku
entries.author: Hagio Moto
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. Vampires who do not age, told out of chronological order across centuries, in a girls' magazine — and the standard reference for the…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Vampires who do not age, told out of chronological order across centuries, in a girls' magazine — and the standard reference for the transformation's formal apparatus. Time is layered rather than sequential, with memory and present sharing a page and panel borders dissolving where the distinction stops mattering, which is `page-4`'s broken frame used as a tense rather than as decoration.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: ベルサイユのばら / Berusaiyu no Bara
entries.author: Ikeda Riyoko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Weekly serial. The French Revolution as shōjo melodrama, built around a woman raised as a man in the royal guard, and the work that made the…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The French Revolution as shōjo melodrama, built around a woman raised as a man in the royal guard, and the work that made the category a mass market rather than a girls' one. The achievement is that neither half is decorative: the history is researched and the romance is why anyone is reading, and the serial declines to treat that combination as a compromise. `page-13`'s tall figure panel is its standing emotional instrument.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: トーマの心臓 / Tōma no Shinzō
entries.author: Hagio Moto
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Weekly serial. A German boarding school, a boy's suicide and the letter he leaves — published in a girls' weekly in 1974. It is the clearest single…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A German boarding school, a boy's suicide and the letter he leaves — published in a girls' weekly in 1974. It is the clearest single answer to anyone who believes the shōjo magazines of the period were constrained in subject matter: the constraint was the page count and the survey, not the material. `psychology-4`'s construction case is the reading experience, because the work rebuilds its situation model twice.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: はいからさんが通る / Haikara-san ga Tōru
entries.author: Yamato Waki
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Weekly serial. A Taishō-era romantic comedy about a modern girl and an army officer, and one of the period's largest commercial successes. It…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A Taishō-era romantic comedy about a modern girl and an army officer, and one of the period's largest commercial successes. It carries colonial-period Manchuria material as setting, which the record requires be named rather than passed over: the romance is staged inside an imperial arrangement the work treats as background. `checklist-13` is the audit and the pack does not adjudicate the work's treatment.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: 風と木の詩 / Kaze to Ki no Uta
entries.author: Takemiya Keiko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Weekly serial. The serial about love between boys that its creator negotiated with editors for years before it ran, and which opened the commercial…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The serial about love between boys that its creator negotiated with editors for years before it ran, and which opened the commercial space the BL category later occupied. **It depicts sexual content involving a minor protagonist**, and both facts belong on the card: its historical importance to the category is real, and the content is what it is. `history-21` states the jurisdictional divergence on drawn material; this pack states it as a fact about jurisdictions and uses it as neither defence nor indictment.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: ガラスの仮面 / Garasu no Kamen
entries.author: Miuchi Suzue
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A teenage actress, a rival, a mask — begun in 1976 and **still unfinished**, which makes it the pack's longest open serialisation…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A teenage actress, a rival, a mask — begun in 1976 and **still unfinished**, which makes it the pack's longest open serialisation case and the live demonstration of `psychology-12`'s ending problem. Fifty years of accumulated reader investment cannot be discharged by a final chapter, and the work's intermittent publication has become part of what readers have a relationship with.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: 地球へ… / Terra e…
entries.author: Takemiya Keiko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. Science fiction in a boys' magazine by a creator central to the shōjo transformation — the transfer running in the direction the…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Science fiction in a boys' magazine by a creator central to the shōjo transformation — the transfer running in the direction the standard account rarely describes. The title is Japanese script read as a Latin word and catalogues render it three ways, which is why the roster pins the printed form. Read beside `work-11`: the experimental page vocabulary reached mainstream SF through creators, not through magazines.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: 綿の国星 / Wata no Kuni Hoshi
entries.author: Ōshima Yumiko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A kitten who believes she is a human girl, drawn as a girl with cat ears and never resolved either way, in a serial that abandons…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A kitten who believes she is a human girl, drawn as a girl with cat ears and never resolved either way, in a serial that abandons plot for psychological state. The formal move is interior monologue running free of any panel, so the page reads as thought with pictures rather than pictures with captions. The creator's name generates Oshima, Ohshima and Ōshima across the record; the pack holds one form.

entries.category: The 1970s Shōjo Revolution
entries.name: 日出処の天子 / Hi Izuru Tokoro no Tenshi
entries.author: Yamagishi Ryōko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A historical serial giving Shōtoku Taishi supernatural power and an unreciprocated love for another man. **The figure has live…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A historical serial giving Shōtoku Taishi supernatural power and an unreciprocated love for another man. **The figure has live religious and national significance**, and the card states that the work is a fictional reading rather than a claim about the historical person — which is the distinction `checklist-13` asks for and the one popular summaries collapse. The pack states the reading and does not adjudicate the objections to it.

entries.category: Shōjo Romance and the Confession Structure
entries.name: ホットロード / Hot Road
entries.author: Tsumugi Taku
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A fourteen-year-old girl, a motorcycle gang and a mother she cannot talk to, told in fragments with more white space than incident.…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A fourteen-year-old girl, a motorcycle gang and a mother she cannot talk to, told in fragments with more white space than incident. It is the shōjo page at its most withholding: whole pages carry a single line of interior monologue, and the reader supplies the rest. `page-24`'s argument that white is not empty has no better case in the collection.

entries.category: Shōjo Romance and the Confession Structure
entries.name: 美少女戦士セーラームーン / Sailor Moon
entries.author: Takeuchi Naoko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. The magical-girl transformation fused with the team-battle structure — a combination neither category had used — and one of the…
entries.text: Monthly serial. The magical-girl transformation fused with the team-battle structure — a combination neither category had used — and one of the medium's largest international properties. `trope-41` cards the transformation as ritual and `psychology-13` explains why the repeated sequence is load-bearing rather than filler. Superhero cards this work from the battle-structure side; here it is a shōjo serial in a girls' monthly, and the battle structure is the import.

entries.category: Shōjo Romance and the Confession Structure
entries.name: ママレード・ボーイ / Marmalade Boy
entries.author: Yoshizumi Wataru |
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. Two teenagers whose parents remarry across the pair, in a relational grid deliberately more complicated than the category had…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Two teenagers whose parents remarry across the pair, in a relational grid deliberately more complicated than the category had carried. The craft interest is bookkeeping: every character's state is tracked and updated each chapter, which is what lets the plot be that tangled without becoming confusing. `trope-27`'s relational grid is this serial's engine.

entries.category: Shōjo Romance and the Confession Structure
entries.name: 花より男子 / Hana yori Dango
entries.author: Kamio Yōko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Weekly serial. A scholarship student against four wealthy boys, running for a decade and adapted across Asia more widely than almost any other…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A scholarship student against four wealthy boys, running for a decade and adapted across Asia more widely than almost any other manga. The obstacle is money and status and stays money and status, which is why the structure travelled to markets whose romance conventions differ from Japan's. **男子 here is read *dango*, not *danshi*** — a standing romanisation trap the roster holds.

entries.category: Shōjo Romance and the Confession Structure
entries.name: こどものおもちゃ / Kodomo no Omocha
entries.author: Obana Miho |
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A child actress, broad comedy, and — in the same pages and without a change of register — neglect, bullying and a mother's…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A child actress, broad comedy, and — in the same pages and without a change of register — neglect, bullying and a mother's withdrawal. The tonal simultaneity is the technique: the joke and the injury occupy one page rather than alternating, with the drawing carrying the second register while the dialogue carries the first.

entries.category: Shōjo Romance and the Confession Structure
entries.name: カードキャプターさくら / Cardcaptor Sakura
entries.author: CLAMP
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A magical-girl serial by a collective, at the point where the group's shōjo work reached its widest readership. `author-13` cards…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A magical-girl serial by a collective, at the point where the group's shōjo work reached its widest readership. `author-13` cards the circle and `serial-64` cards the pipeline that produced it. The title mixes katakana and hiragana, and the English release title is the standard search form — a divergence the roster records rather than resolves.

entries.category: Shōjo Romance and the Confession Structure
entries.name: 花ざかりの君たちへ / Hanazakari no Kimitachi e
entries.author: Nakajo Hisaya |
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A girl enrols at a boys' school in disguise, and the serial spends hundreds of chapters on being read as the wrong thing. The…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A girl enrols at a boys' school in disguise, and the serial spends hundreds of chapters on being read as the wrong thing. The discipline is farce discipline: the rules of the disguise are fixed early and never bent for authorial convenience, so every scene's tension comes from the rules. `trope-46`'s changed body in a comic register.

entries.category: Shōjo Romance and the Confession Structure
entries.name: フルーツバスケット / Fruits Basket
entries.author: Takaya Natsuki |
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A family cursed to transform into zodiac animals, used as an armature for material about abuse, isolation and recovery. It is the…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A family cursed to transform into zodiac animals, used as an armature for material about abuse, isolation and recovery. It is the strongest case in the collection for a genre premise as a delivery system: the curse is a comedy device in chapter one and the mechanism by which the work discusses damage by chapter eighty. `trope-43`'s bargained-with beast, extended across a whole serial.

entries.category: Shōjo Romance and the Confession Structure
entries.name: 君に届け / Kimi ni Todoke
entries.author: Shiina Karuho
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. The contemporary reference case for the confession structure: a straightforward premise extended over years by treating every small…
entries.text: Monthly serial. The contemporary reference case for the confession structure: a straightforward premise extended over years by treating every small misreading as a full event. A single conversation can occupy a chapter, with interior monologue and drawn pause doing the work plot does elsewhere. `trope-25` cards the dated confession and `trope-26` the deferral; this is the extreme execution of both without cheating.

entries.category: Josei and the Adult Woman's Register
entries.name: あさきゆめみし / Asaki Yumemishi
entries.author: Yamato Waki
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. The Tale of Genji adapted at length for a women's readership, running to 1993 and used in Japanese schools as an entry to the…
entries.text: Monthly serial. The Tale of Genji adapted at length for a women's readership, running to 1993 and used in Japanese schools as an entry to the original. The craft question it answers is how to adapt a text whose interest is psychological and whose plot is thin: the answer is to let the page carry interiority and to keep the incident rate low, which the shōjo apparatus was already built to do.

entries.category: Josei and the Adult Woman's Register
entries.name: ハッピー・マニア / Happy Mania
entries.author: Anno Moyoco
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A woman in her twenties pursuing relationships with a compulsiveness the serial declines to make charming, running to 2001. The line…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A woman in her twenties pursuing relationships with a compulsiveness the serial declines to make charming, running to 2001. The line itself is restless — hatching and motion where another artist would use stillness — and matched to a protagonist who cannot stop, so the style and the subject are the same observation twice. The josei register at its least consoling.

entries.category: Josei and the Adult Woman's Register
entries.name: NANA
entries.author: Yazawa Ai
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. Two women with the same name, in Tokyo, with bands, clothes and money — and **on indefinite hiatus since 2009**, which makes it a…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Two women with the same name, in Tokyo, with bands, clothes and money — and **on indefinite hiatus since 2009**, which makes it a live serialisation case rather than a completed work. Clothes function as characterisation with a designer's specificity, so a change of outfit is a change of state. The title is Latin in the original, which the roster holds because the romanised half is the whole name.

entries.category: Josei and the Adult Woman's Register
entries.name: ハチミツとクローバー / Hachimitsu to Clover
entries.author: Umino Chica
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. Art students, unrequited love in a closed circle, and the ordinary terror of graduating without a plan. It is also the pack's…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Art students, unrequited love in a closed circle, and the ordinary terror of graduating without a plan. It is also the pack's magazine-transfer case: the serial moved publications when its original magazine folded, which `craft-53` treats as a craft problem and which the roster records because the venue is plural for a reason.

entries.category: Josei and the Adult Woman's Register
entries.name: 大奥 / Ōoku
entries.author: Yoshinaga Fumi
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. An Edo in which a plague has killed most men and the shogunate is female, worked out as political history rather than as a premise.…
entries.text: Monthly serial. An Edo in which a plague has killed most men and the shogunate is female, worked out as political history rather than as a premise. Whole chapters are two people talking while doing something ordinary, with the argument carried inside the exchange — the method `author-46` cards. The title romanises three ways and the roster pins one, per pass N's `oo` generator.

entries.category: Josei and the Adult Woman's Register
entries.name: 海街diary / Umimachi Diary
entries.author: Yoshida Akimi
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. Four sisters in a seaside town, told at the pace of seasons, with emotional events staged in the flattest possible way so the reader…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Four sisters in a seaside town, told at the pace of seasons, with emotional events staged in the flattest possible way so the reader does the arithmetic. The restraint reads as confidence rather than as withholding. The title mixes kanji and Latin in the original, which the roster holds rather than normalising.

entries.category: Josei and the Adult Woman's Register
entries.name: 東京タラレバ娘 / Tokyo Tarareba Musume
entries.author: Higashimura Akiko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Weekly serial. Three women in their thirties discovering that the plan they had was not a plan, written with an autobiographical looseness that made…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Three women in their thirties discovering that the plan they had was not a plan, written with an autobiographical looseness that made the essay register commercially central to josei. The drawing is fast and leaves its correction lines in, which reads as candour and lets a chapter turn from farce to something painful without a visible seam.

entries.category: Josei and the Adult Woman's Register
entries.name: 凪のお暇 / Nagi no Oitoma
entries.author: Konari Misato |
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. A woman quits her job, her relationship and her flat after a breakdown and rebuilds slowly, with no romantic resolution as the…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A woman quits her job, her relationship and her flat after a breakdown and rebuilds slowly, with no romantic resolution as the object and no return to the starting arrangement. Recovery is legible through logistics — rent, the fridge, the neighbours — rather than through declaration, which is `trope-62`'s everyday density used for psychological state.

entries.category: BL, Yaoi and Yuri
entries.name: 白い部屋のふたり / Shiroi Heya no Futari
entries.author: Yamagishi Ryōko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. Widely described as the first shōjo manga with a lesbian couple at its centre, and the origin point most accounts of yuri begin…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Widely described as the first shōjo manga with a lesbian couple at its centre, and the origin point most accounts of yuri begin from. **The 1971 date and the venue rest on secondary sources** and the pack states that rather than presenting them as established. `subgenre-24`'s two lineages start here on one side, and `author-32` is the creator the narrow Year 24 roster leaves out.

entries.category: BL, Yaoi and Yuri
entries.name: 絶愛-1989- / Zetsuai -1989-
entries.author: Ozaki Minami
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. The commercial serialisation that came directly out of the self-published circuit and demonstrated a market the publishers were not…
entries.text: Monthly serial. The commercial serialisation that came directly out of the self-published circuit and demonstrated a market the publishers were not serving. Melodrama at maximum intensity, with shōjo's decorative apparatus used at a pitch the shōjo magazines would not have permitted. **The year is inside the title**, which the roster flags because a year-extraction pass will read it as data.

entries.category: BL, Yaoi and Yuri
entries.name: 純情ロマンチカ / Junjō Romantica
entries.author: Nakamura Shungiku |
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. One of the two long parallel serials that established BL as an ongoing commercial property rather than a single-volume category. The…
entries.text: Monthly serial. One of the two long parallel serials that established BL as an ongoing commercial property rather than a single-volume category. The structural move is that the couples are stable and the incident comes from the workplace, which is what makes the serials extendable at all — `trope-29`'s relationship that continues past the yes, running as a business model.

entries.category: BL, Yaoi and Yuri
entries.name: 青い花 / Aoi Hana
entries.author: Shimura Takako
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. Girls in love with girls, written as ordinary adolescence and published in a general magazine rather than a category title. The…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Girls in love with girls, written as ordinary adolescence and published in a general magazine rather than a category title. The pacing is very quiet and the significant moment is placed in an unemphatic panel and left there; the refusal of emphasis is the ethical position as much as the style. `page-12`'s duration lever, used by declining to spend it.

entries.category: BL, Yaoi and Yuri
entries.name: 同級生 / Dōkyūsei
entries.author: Nakamura Asumiko
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Volume-first work. Two boys, a school choir, and a restraint unusual in the category — elongated figures, wide margins, long silences, with the…
entries.text: Volume-first work. Two boys, a school choir, and a restraint unusual in the category — elongated figures, wide margins, long silences, with the erotic content present and not the engine. **The magazine serialisation's start year could not be established**, so the card is dated by the volume and says so. The title is also the title of unrelated works, which the roster records.

entries.category: BL, Yaoi and Yuri
entries.name: 世界一初恋 / Sekai-ichi Hatsukoi
entries.author: Nakamura Shungiku
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. The parallel serial to `work-65`, set in a manga editorial department — a BL serial whose workplace is the industry this pack…
entries.text: Monthly serial. The parallel serial to `work-65`, set in a manga editorial department — a BL serial whose workplace is the industry this pack describes. It ran across three magazines from the start, so its venue is plural by design rather than by transfer, which is the distinction `craft-53` turns on.

entries.category: BL, Yaoi and Yuri
entries.name: あさがおと加瀬さん。 / Asagao to Kase-san.
entries.author: Takashima Hiromi
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Anthology serial. Two schoolgirls already in a relationship, spending the serial on ordinary days rather than on getting together — the genre's…
entries.text: Anthology serial. Two schoolgirls already in a relationship, spending the serial on ordinary days rather than on getting together — the genre's usual engine removed and replaced with domestic incident. It began as a one-shot and became a serial, and **the trailing 。 is part of the title**, which the roster holds because punctuation is where a title quietly loses a character.

entries.category: BL, Yaoi and Yuri
entries.name: やがて君になる / Yagate Kimi ni Naru
entries.author: Nakatani Nio
entries.awards: No award is asserted on this card.
entries.description: Monthly serial. One protagonist cannot feel romantic attraction and the other loves her anyway — the category's central convention taken up and…
entries.text: Monthly serial. One protagonist cannot feel romantic attraction and the other loves her anyway — the category's central convention taken up and refused. It ran in a magazine with a male-skewing readership, which is `checklist-8`'s demographic point in a single line: the audience a work reaches is not the category its content belongs to.

entries.category: Antecedents: Newspaper Strip and the Prewar Children's Magazine
entries.name: ジャパン・パンチ / The Japan Punch
entries.author: Charles Wirgman
entries.awards: None; the prize system is eighty years away.
entries.description: Anthology serial. The foreign-language satirical monthly produced in Yokohama from 1862, and the object through which the modern cartoon's…
entries.text: Anthology serial. The foreign-language satirical monthly produced in Yokohama from 1862, and the object through which the modern cartoon's conventions entered Japan — the single panel, the caricatured public figure, the caption, the periodical schedule. The word *ponchi* entering Japanese as a term for a cartoon is the clearest evidence of the direction of transmission, and `history-5` cards it. **There is no Japanese 原題**: the title is English and the katakana form is the standard Japanese rendering rather than an original, which the roster records because a name with no source-language form breaks the pack's own naming rule and has to say so.

entries.category: Antecedents: Newspaper Strip and the Prewar Children's Magazine
entries.name: 田吾作と杢兵衛の東京見物 / Tagosaku to Mokubē no Tokyo Kenbutsu
entries.author: Kitazawa Rakuten
entries.description: Newspaper strip. Two countrymen visit Tokyo, in the strip usually named as the first in the Western sense to run in a Japanese newspaper. **The…
entries.text: Newspaper strip. Two countrymen visit Tokyo, in the strip usually named as the first in the Western sense to run in a Japanese newspaper. **The claim around its author — that he is the first modern Japanese manga artist — is contested**, and the dispute is the continuity argument in miniature: whether the profession begins here with an imported form, or continues a native tradition through it. `history-4` and `author-118` carry both sides; this card states the work and the claim about it separately.

entries.category: Antecedents: Newspaper Strip and the Prewar Children's Magazine
entries.name: 東京パック / Tokyo Puck
entries.author: Kitazawa Rakuten
entries.description: Anthology serial. A colour cartoon magazine founded in 1905 and named for the American *Puck*, carded as a body of work rather than as a single…
entries.text: Anthology serial. A colour cartoon magazine founded in 1905 and named for the American *Puck*, carded as a body of work rather than as a single strip because that is what it is: one artist's satirical output at mass circulation, on a schedule, for a paying readership. `history-6` argues that the newspaper made the recurring character and `history-8` that the profession precedes the art form; this magazine is where both become visible at once.

entries.category: Antecedents: Newspaper Strip and the Prewar Children's Magazine
entries.name: 正チヤンの冒険 / Shō-chan no Bōken
entries.author: Oda Shōsei (writer) · Kabashima Katsuichi, as Tōfūjin (artist)
entries.description: Newspaper strip. A boy and a squirrel, in the 1923 strip where the parts assemble: a continuing narrative rather than a gag, speech inside balloons…
entries.text: Newspaper strip. A boy and a squirrel, in the 1923 strip where the parts assemble: a continuing narrative rather than a gag, speech inside balloons rather than captions below the frame, and collection into a book almost immediately. `history-7` cards the assembly and `serial-41` the consequence — the two-object economy of serial and volume is present from the beginning. **The title has three printed forms**, one of them with large kana, which is why the roster pins one and records the others.

entries.category: Antecedents: Newspaper Strip and the Prewar Children's Magazine
entries.name: のらくろ / Norakuro
entries.author: Tagawa Suihō
entries.description: Monthly serial. A stray dog enlists, and the strip becomes the defining children's serial of the 1930s. Its character design is built for instant…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A stray dog enlists, and the strip becomes the defining children's serial of the 1930s. Its character design is built for instant recognition and reuse, which is `craft-34`'s merchandise logic decades early. **The run tracks Japan's expanding war and the strip served it**, and the craft and the function belong on the same card — `history-10` states the same account at period level and §6 requires that neither half be omitted for the comfort of the other. The first instalment ran under a longer title, which the roster holds.

entries.category: Antecedents: Newspaper Strip and the Prewar Children's Magazine
entries.name: 冒険ダン吉 / Bōken Dankichi
entries.author: Shimada Keizō
entries.description: Monthly serial. A Japanese boy becomes king of a South Seas island, in a hugely popular 1930s children's serial whose depiction of the islanders is…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A Japanese boy becomes king of a South Seas island, in a hugely popular 1930s children's serial whose depiction of the islanders is racial caricature. **Postwar criticism reads it as glorifying expansionism**, and Kawamura Minato's reading treats the visual system as colonial and Orientalist rather than incidentally offensive. `history-11` carries the argument; this card carries the work and states that its popularity and its caricature are the same object. `checklist-13` is the audit.

entries.category: Antecedents: Newspaper Strip and the Prewar Children's Magazine
entries.name: タンクタンクロー / Tanku Tankurō
entries.author: Sakamoto Gajō
entries.description: Monthly serial. A round armoured figure who produces weapons from his own body, running to the end of 1936 and often cited as the first Japanese…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A round armoured figure who produces weapons from his own body, running to the end of 1936 and often cited as the first Japanese robot manga. The claim is worth holding loosely — it depends on what counts as a robot — but the design logic is not in doubt: a character built as a shape, for recognition, in a children's monthly whose commercial apparatus `history-9` describes as the real ancestor of the postwar system.

entries.category: Tezuka and the Story-Manga Form
entries.name: 新宝島 / Shin Takarajima
entries.author: Sakai Shichima (concept/structure) · Tezuka Osamu (art)
entries.description: Volume-first work. The 1947 akahon volume conventionally treated as the postwar turning point, and **the credit is disputed in the scholarship**:…
entries.text: Volume-first work. The 1947 akahon volume conventionally treated as the postwar turning point, and **the credit is disputed in the scholarship**: Nakano Haruyuki credits Sakai Shichima with the concept and structure, other accounts treat the work as substantially Tezuka's. The pack states the dispute and adjudicates nothing — `author-66` cards the collaborator whose name disappears from popular accounts, and `history-13` carries the contested cinematic-technique claim this volume is the usual evidence for. The first edition prints the title with the older character form.

entries.category: Tezuka and the Story-Manga Form
entries.name: ジャングル大帝 / Jungle Taitei
entries.author: Tezuka Osamu
entries.description: Monthly serial. A long-form animal narrative in a children's monthly, and an early demonstration that a manga serial could sustain a single story…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A long-form animal narrative in a children's monthly, and an early demonstration that a manga serial could sustain a single story across years rather than a strip's worth of incidents. Two English variants circulate and **one of them is anime-derived rather than this work's title**, which the roster separates because an adaptation's name attaching to its source is a standing phantom-duplicate generator.

entries.category: Tezuka and the Story-Manga Form
entries.name: 鉄腕アトム / Tetsuwan Atomu
entries.author: Tezuka Osamu
entries.description: Monthly serial. The robot boy serial that ran for seventeen years and became the medium's most exported early property. Its production conditions…
entries.text: Monthly serial. The robot boy serial that ran for seventeen years and became the medium's most exported early property. Its production conditions are as important as its content: this is the work whose animation deal set the price structure the adaptation economy inherited, which `serial-58` and `craft-30` both reach back to. The 1951 precursor is a different title and is deliberately not carded, and the two English names are recorded rather than merged.

entries.category: Tezuka and the Story-Manga Form
entries.name: 火の鳥 / Hi no Tori
entries.author: Tezuka Osamu
entries.description: Monthly serial. The unfinished cycle its author returned to across four decades, moving between magazines and formats. **The 1967 COM version is the…
entries.text: Monthly serial. The unfinished cycle its author returned to across four decades, moving between magazines and formats. **The 1967 COM version is the one most readers mean and the 1954 appearance is the one the year records** — the roster holds the first appearance per `checklist-15`, which means the date on this card will look wrong to anyone who knows the famous version. `serial-69` cards the laboratory magazine the later version ran in.

entries.category: Tezuka and the Story-Manga Form
entries.name: 奇子 / Ayako
entries.author: Tezuka Osamu
entries.description: Monthly serial. A landowning family in Occupation-era Japan, built on confinement, incest and political violence, published for an adult readership.…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A landowning family in Occupation-era Japan, built on confinement, incest and political violence, published for an adult readership. **The content is stated and neither endorsed nor condemned**, which is the §6 posture: a reference work that carded this author's children's serials and passed over the adult work would be describing a career that did not happen. `checklist-14` is the audit for any writer drawing on it.

entries.category: Tezuka and the Story-Manga Form
entries.name: ブラック・ジャック / Black Jack
entries.author: Tezuka Osamu
entries.description: Weekly serial. An unlicensed surgeon, one case per chapter, produced under weekly survey pressure — the pack's principal case for the self-contained…
entries.text: Weekly serial. An unlicensed surgeon, one case per chapter, produced under weekly survey pressure — the pack's principal case for the self-contained chapter as a survival structure. `craft-9`'s arc that can be cut short and `serial-32`'s compressed ending both point here: an episodic serial has no arc to truncate, which is precisely why the format is chosen under that pressure rather than in spite of it.

entries.category: Tezuka and the Story-Manga Form
entries.name: アドルフに告ぐ / Adolf ni Tsugu
entries.author: Tezuka Osamu
entries.description: Weekly serial. Three men named Adolf, across Kobe, Berlin and the war, serialised in a general-interest weekly rather than a manga magazine. **It…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Three men named Adolf, across Kobe, Berlin and the war, serialised in a general-interest weekly rather than a manga magazine. **It carries Holocaust and wartime-Japan content and a fictional claim about a historical head of state**, and the card states that the claim is the work's invention rather than a historical assertion — the distinction `checklist-12` asks for and popular summaries collapse.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: 仮面ライダー / Kamen Rider
entries.author: Ishinomori Shōtarō
entries.description: Weekly serial. The manga half of a dual-origin property, and **it diverges sharply from the television series it shares a name with** — darker,…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The manga half of a dual-origin property, and **it diverges sharply from the television series it shares a name with** — darker, bleaker, and ending differently. That divergence is the card's reason for existing: the pack cards the manga, the television series is declined to TV Formats with a stated reason, and `craft-33`'s adaptation-that-overtakes-the-source runs in both directions here. It discharges the Superhero debt subject whose suffix that pack added and `debt_work_key()` strips.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: 北斗の拳 / Hokuto no Ken
entries.author: Buronson (story) · Hara Tetsuo (art)
entries.description: Weekly serial. A post-apocalyptic martial-arts serial built on an escalating opponent ladder, written by one person and drawn by another — the…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A post-apocalyptic martial-arts serial built on an escalating opponent ladder, written by one person and drawn by another — the writer-artist split `craft-48` cards and `author-112` and `author-113` card from both sides. Its violence set the decade's register for shōnen, and its structure is `trope-16`'s ladder in the form later serials had to answer.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: ドラゴンボール / Dragon Ball
entries.author: Toriyama Akira
entries.description: Weekly serial. **The pack's central example of the survey changing a work mid-serialisation**: a gag adventure that turns into a…
entries.text: Weekly serial. **The pack's central example of the survey changing a work mid-serialisation**: a gag adventure that turns into a tournament-and-escalation serial, with the editorial pressure documented by both the creator and his editor. `history-3` cards the case, `serial-53` cards the mechanism, and `author-108` cards the editor who holds no credit on any of it. Everything this pack argues about the weekly system is legible in one serial's change of direction.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: 聖闘士星矢 / Seinto Seiya
entries.author: Kurumada Masami
entries.description: Weekly serial. Armoured protagonists, constellation designs, and a toy line planned with the fiction rather than after it — `craft-34`'s merchandise…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Armoured protagonists, constellation designs, and a toy line planned with the fiction rather than after it — `craft-34`'s merchandise logic sitting in the premise rather than arriving as a consequence. **The title is a romanisation trap**: 聖闘士 is printed with furigana reading セイント, so the work reads *Saint Seiya*, which no romanisation of the kanji produces. The roster holds both halves for exactly that reason.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: るろうに剣心 -明治剣客浪漫譚- / Rurouni Kenshin -Meiji Kenkaku Romantan-
entries.author: Watsuki Nobuhiro
entries.description: Weekly serial. A Meiji-era swordsman who has renounced killing, in a genre built on escalation — a constraint that forces fights to be solved rather…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A Meiji-era swordsman who has renounced killing, in a genre built on escalation — a constraint that forces fights to be solved rather than won. **The creator was charged in 2017 and fined in 2018 by summary disposition over possession of child pornography; serialisation resumed in June 2018, and the English-market response diverged from the Japanese one.** Neither "convicted" as an English reader is likely to infer it nor "cleared" is accurate, and this card states the disposition rather than a characterisation of it. The pack's Creators roster does not carry him — an omission recorded in the build log at §3.26 — and §6 requires the case be handled, so it is handled here.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: ONE PIECE
entries.author: Oda Eiichirō
entries.description: Weekly serial. The longest-running serial of the modern weekly era and the highest-selling, with a stated endpoint declared early and an enormous…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The longest-running serial of the modern weekly era and the highest-selling, with a stated endpoint declared early and an enormous cast introduced across decades. `psychology-15`'s memory problem is its standing risk and it manages it by restaging rather than by assuming recall. **The printed title is Latin with no Japanese 原題**, and the roster records that every letter in it is a Latin codepoint — the homoglyph check `page`-side screen 29c exists for.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: HUNTER×HUNTER
entries.author: Togashi Yoshihiro
entries.description: Weekly serial. A battle serial that spends chapters on negotiation, strategy and rule-explanation where the format expects a fight, and whose…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A battle serial that spends chapters on negotiation, strategy and rule-explanation where the format expects a fight, and whose **repeated multi-year hiatuses are part of the record rather than gossip** — the clearest live case of `serial-13`'s rhythms being what a career is actually built on. The separator in the title is a multiplication sign rather than the letter x, which the roster pins because the two are indistinguishable at reading size.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: NARUTO -ナルト- / Naruto
entries.author: Kishimoto Masashi
entries.description: Weekly serial. A ninja serial whose techniques form an explicit, learnable system with stated costs — `trope-13`'s tier list and `trope-19`'s named…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A ninja serial whose techniques form an explicit, learnable system with stated costs — `trope-13`'s tier list and `trope-19`'s named cost at their most disciplined — and among the first Jump serials whose international readership was visibly part of its commercial life during serialisation. **This build already caught a Cyrillic Н standing in for the N of NARUTO once**, which is why screen 29c exists and why the roster states that every letter here is Latin.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: 鋼の錬金術師 / Hagane no Renkinjutsushi
entries.author: Arakawa Hiromu
entries.description: Monthly serial. A shōnen serial with a fixed central law honoured from the first chapter, a stated endpoint, and an ending reached on schedule — the…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A shōnen serial with a fixed central law honoured from the first chapter, a stated endpoint, and an ending reached on schedule — the standing counter-example to the format's extension pressure that `serial-31` describes. It is monthly rather than weekly, published outside the largest boys' weekly, and written by a woman, and all three are worth noticing before treating the shōnen category as one thing. The English abbreviation generates the five-variant pattern the roster names.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: 進撃の巨人 / Attack on Titan
entries.author: Isayama Hajime
entries.description: Monthly serial. A monthly serial that became the decade's largest international manga property, built on information withheld for years and then…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A monthly serial that became the decade's largest international manga property, built on information withheld for years and then delivered as a reframing rather than a reveal — `page-8`'s withholding at the scale of a whole work. **Its conclusion was received with unusual public disagreement**, which the card states without ruling on, and `psychology-12` explains structurally why a decade of accumulation is not dischargeable by a final chapter. **A second and larger dispute attaches to the work and to its author's social-media statements**: readings of the serial as militarist or as an argument about the wartime past are argued in both directions by people who have read it closely, and the author's own remarks have been read as confirming one side and as being misrepresented. **Positions are on the record and this pack adjudicates none of them.** `checklist-13` and `history-11` are the neighbouring instruments; the title is the canonical five-variant romanisation case.

entries.category: Shōnen Battle and the Weekly System
entries.name: 僕のヒーローアカデミア / My Hero Academia
entries.author: Horikoshi Kōhei
entries.description: Weekly serial. The American superhero premise run on the Japanese school-and-tournament structure — the reverse import `author-73` cards. **A 2020…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The American superhero premise run on the Japanese school-and-tournament structure — the reverse import `author-73` cards. **A 2020 character name was read as a reference to Unit 731 and drew organised objection in China and South Korea**; the creator and publisher apologised and the name was changed. The objection, the apology and the change are all on the record, and this pack states the sequence and adjudicates nothing. `checklist-13` is the instrument.

entries.category: Sports and Spokon
entries.name: 巨人の星 / Kyojin no Hoshi
entries.author: Kajiwara Ikki · Kawasaki Noboru
entries.description: Weekly serial. The spokon template, assembled here and copied for a decade: a father's ambition, a body driven past its limits, and suffering as the…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The spokon template, assembled here and copied for a decade: a father's ambition, a body driven past its limits, and suffering as the mechanism of worth. The writer and artist are separately credited, which `craft-48` cards and which was still uncommon. Read it as period evidence rather than as instruction — `trope-17`'s training sequence and `trope-20`'s body that pays both descend from it, and both have spent fifty years being argued with.

entries.category: Sports and Spokon
entries.name: あしたのジョー / Ashita no Joe
entries.author: Takamori Asao, a pen name of Kajiwara Ikki · Chiba Tetsuya
entries.description: Weekly serial. A boxer from the slums, and the medium's standard reference for an ending — a final image that is a still figure rather than a blow.…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A boxer from the slums, and the medium's standard reference for an ending — a final image that is a still figure rather than a blow. `trope-65`'s death that is not reversed and `craft-14`'s farewell both point here. **The byline is a pen name of a creator this pack cards under another name**, which the roster records: the same writer appears twice in the record under two names, and a naive identity pass merges or splits them wrongly. `checklist-15` is the audit.

entries.category: Sports and Spokon
entries.name: エースをねらえ! / Ace o Nerae!
entries.author: Yamamoto Sumika
entries.description: Weekly serial. The spokon structure — endurance, a withholding mentor, rivalry as intimacy — running in a girls' magazine with a female protagonist,…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The spokon structure — endurance, a withholding mentor, rivalry as intimacy — running in a girls' magazine with a female protagonist, at a scale that made the sports serial a shōjo category too. **Genre and demographic pull apart visibly here**, which is `checklist-8`'s whole point: the material is spokon and the readership is shōjo, and neither fact determines the other.

entries.category: Sports and Spokon
entries.name: SLAM DUNK
entries.author: Inoue Takehiko
entries.description: Weekly serial. A basketball serial that replaced the endurance ideology with technique and team dynamics, and whose late sequences run long…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A basketball serial that replaced the endurance ideology with technique and team dynamics, and whose late sequences run long stretches with no dialogue at all — the silence structural rather than decorative, with reading pace and panel position carrying the tension. `page-15` cites it for exactly that. The printed title is Latin with no Japanese 原題, and appears with and without a space, which the roster pins.

entries.category: Sports and Spokon
entries.name: ちはやふる / Chihayafuru
entries.author: Suetsugu Yuki
entries.description: Weekly serial. Competitive karuta — a card game built on classical poetry — in a josei magazine, and the block's second case of a sports structure…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Competitive karuta — a card game built on classical poetry — in a josei magazine, and the block's second case of a sports structure sitting in a demographic that has nothing to do with sport. The procedural discipline is the achievement: the game is explained completely enough that the reader can follow a match, which is `craft-36`'s procedural contract met in a subject with almost no existing audience.

entries.category: Seinen and the Adult Magazine
entries.name: ゴルゴ13 / Golgo 13
entries.author: Saitō Takao
entries.description: Anthology serial. The medium's longest-running serial, produced on an explicit studio division of labour its principal described publicly and…
entries.text: Anthology serial. The medium's longest-running serial, produced on an explicit studio division of labour its principal described publicly and defended as the correct way to make a long work — the authorship model `serial-58` prices and `author-3` cards. It has continued past his death, which is the model's proof rather than its footnote: a serial that does not stop when one person does is a different kind of object from an authored one.

entries.category: Seinen and the Adult Magazine
entries.name: 三丁目の夕日 / Sanchōme no Yūhi
entries.author: Saigan Ryōhei
entries.description: Anthology serial. Nostalgic vignettes of Shōwa-era Tokyo, running since 1974 and still going — the medium's most sustained exercise in the ordinary…
entries.text: Anthology serial. Nostalgic vignettes of Shōwa-era Tokyo, running since 1974 and still going — the medium's most sustained exercise in the ordinary past as subject. **The title is now printed in an extended form and the 1974 bare form is what the roster carries**, with both in current use, which is the moving-title problem `checklist-15` audits and which no amount of care at drafting time can prevent if the roster is not the authority.

entries.category: Seinen and the Adult Magazine
entries.name: 課長島耕作 / Kachō Shima Kōsaku
entries.author: Hirokane Kenshi
entries.description: Anthology serial. A corporate employee's career followed across decades of real-time promotion, which made the workplace a durable seinen category —…
entries.text: Anthology serial. A corporate employee's career followed across decades of real-time promotion, which made the workplace a durable seinen category — `trope-59`'s work as the source of incident, in its founding case. **The rank in the title changes with each successor series**, so the title is a moving target by design; the roster carries the first form and records the pattern.

entries.category: Seinen and the Adult Magazine
entries.name: 沈黙の艦隊 / Chinmoku no Kantai
entries.author: Kawaguchi Kaiji
entries.description: Weekly serial. A Japanese nuclear-armed submarine crew declares independence, in a serial read in Japan as an argument about the Self-Defense Forces…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A Japanese nuclear-armed submarine crew declares independence, in a serial read in Japan as an argument about the Self-Defense Forces and the postwar constitutional settlement rather than only as a thriller. **It was debated as a political proposition in the national press**, and both the reading that it is a serious constitutional argument and the reading that it is a nationalist fantasy are held by serious people. The pack states the dispute and does not settle it.

entries.category: Seinen and the Adult Magazine
entries.name: 寄生獣 / Kiseijū
entries.author: Iwaaki Hitoshi
entries.description: Monthly serial. A parasite takes over a boy's right hand and they negotiate a coexistence — a horror premise worked through as a question about what…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A parasite takes over a boy's right hand and they negotiate a coexistence — a horror premise worked through as a question about what a person owes other species. `trope-44`'s uninvited passenger is this work carded. **It is commonly dated 1988 and the record is 1989**, with the two-magazine start the reason for the drift; the roster holds the later date and this card says why.

entries.category: Seinen and the Adult Magazine
entries.name: MONSTER
entries.author: Urasawa Naoki
entries.description: Weekly serial. A suspense serial built on a question posed early and deferred for years, carried almost entirely by ordinary faces in close panels…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A suspense serial built on a question posed early and deferred for years, carried almost entirely by ordinary faces in close panels rather than by incident. `page-8`'s withholding is its working method at the scale of a whole serial, and `psychology-14`'s point about readers rehearsing their own answers between instalments is the risk it runs deliberately. The printed title is Latin with no Japanese 原題.

entries.category: Seinen and the Adult Magazine
entries.name: 蟲師 / Mushishi
entries.author: 漆原友紀 Urushibara Yuki |
entries.description: Monthly serial. A travelling specialist encounters spirit-like organisms, in near-standalone chapters with generous inter-panel space and almost no…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A travelling specialist encounters spirit-like organisms, in near-standalone chapters with generous inter-panel space and almost no dramatic escalation. `page-11` cites it for gutter width as a duration cue: the reading pace is measurably slower than a battle serial's with no change in the amount of incident, which is the clearest demonstration in the collection that pace is a design decision rather than a consequence of content.

entries.category: Seinen and the Adult Magazine
entries.name: 岳 みんなの山 / Gaku: Minna no Yama
entries.author: Ishizuka Shinichi
entries.description: Anthology serial. Mountain rescue, researched to a standard mountaineering readers accept, with human figures held small inside large frames so the…
entries.text: Anthology serial. Mountain rescue, researched to a standard mountaineering readers accept, with human figures held small inside large frames so the mountain does the measuring — `page-20`'s downward scale as a book's central argument. **It is frequently cited as bare 岳**, which is a common noun and will collide with anything; the roster carries the full form for that reason.

entries.category: Seinen and the Adult Magazine
entries.name: 闇金ウシジマくん / Yamikin Ushijima-kun
entries.author: Manabe Shōhei
entries.description: Weekly serial. An illegal moneylender and the people who borrow from him, in a rotating case structure where most borrowers are destroyed. **It…
entries.text: Weekly serial. An illegal moneylender and the people who borrow from him, in a rotating case structure where most borrowers are destroyed. **It depicts illegal lending, sex work and organised crime in a documentary register**, with the misery presented as arithmetic — interest rates, collection practice, exact sums — rather than as tragedy. `trope-60`'s client of the week, run without the mercy the format usually supplies. `checklist-14` applies to any writer working this material.

entries.category: Horror Manga
entries.name: ゲゲゲの鬼太郎 / Gegege no Kitarō
entries.author: Mizuki Shigeru
entries.description: Weekly serial. The yōkai serial that made folklore a permanent manga genre, with photographically dense backgrounds and cartoon figures moving…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The yōkai serial that made folklore a permanent manga genre, with photographically dense backgrounds and cartoon figures moving through them — the visual argument that the supernatural is ordinary. **The same character's kashihon incarnation is carded separately as `work-4`**, and the two are different works in different markets with different registers. This pack's own Creator collection merged them once before screen 33 caught it.

entries.category: Horror Manga
entries.name: 漂流教室 / Hyōryū Kyōshitsu
entries.author: Umezu Kazuo
entries.description: Weekly serial. A primary school and everyone in it is transported to a wasteland, published in a children's weekly, at an intensity adult horror…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A primary school and everyone in it is transported to a wasteland, published in a children's weekly, at an intensity adult horror rarely reaches. Children die and stay dead. The technique is faces distorted past anatomy at the moment of terror — `page-25`'s register change, telling the reader the rules have gone before a word is read.

entries.category: Horror Manga
entries.name: デビルマン / Devilman
entries.author: Nagai Gō
entries.description: Weekly serial. A demon-possession serial whose ending is among the medium's bleakest, and **the pack's cleanest simultaneous-media case**: the manga…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A demon-possession serial whose ending is among the medium's bleakest, and **the pack's cleanest simultaneous-media case**: the manga and the television anime ran at the same time and diverge completely, with only the manga carded here. `craft-31`'s question of what survives the move to motion is answered here by *almost nothing*, because the two were never versions of each other.

entries.category: Horror Manga
entries.name: 恐怖新聞 / Kyōfu Shinbun
entries.author: Tsunoda Jirō
entries.description: Weekly serial. A newspaper delivers tomorrow's disasters and costs the reader a hundred days of life per issue, running to 1975 across twenty-nine…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A newspaper delivers tomorrow's disasters and costs the reader a hundred days of life per issue, running to 1975 across twenty-nine chapters — a document of the 1970s occult boom as much as a horror serial. The premise is a metered cost, which is `trope-19`'s named cost in its purest form: every instalment spends the same currency and the reader can do the arithmetic.

entries.category: Horror Manga
entries.name: 富江 / Tomie
entries.author: Itō Junji
entries.description: Anthology serial. A woman who cannot be killed and regenerates from any fragment, in a sequence of self-contained stories — a debut built on one…
entries.text: Anthology serial. A woman who cannot be killed and regenerates from any fragment, in a sequence of self-contained stories — a debut built on one rule applied without exception. `psychology-6`'s point about a convention carrying a role with no content applies to its reveals. The year rests on secondary sources; the publisher record was not reached this pass, and the card says so rather than presenting it as established.

entries.category: Horror Manga
entries.name: うずまき / Uzumaki
entries.author: Itō Junji
entries.description: Weekly serial. A town infected by a geometric shape, with the spiral propagating through hair, pottery, bodies and finally architecture. It is the…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A town infected by a geometric shape, with the spiral propagating through hair, pottery, bodies and finally architecture. It is the strongest available demonstration of horror built from a single formal rule rather than from a threat: `horror:craft-11`'s argument that specificity beats magnitude, executed by making the specific thing a shape.

entries.category: SF, Mecha and the Speculative Line
entries.name: 鉄人28号 / Tetsujin 28-gō
entries.author: Yokoyama Mitsuteru
entries.description: Monthly serial. A giant robot controlled from outside by a boy with a box — and the control relation is the point, not the robot. A body that…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A giant robot controlled from outside by a boy with a box — and the control relation is the point, not the robot. A body that transforms proposes one thing about power; a machine somebody else could pick up the controller for proposes another, and the whole mecha line descends from that difference. `page-18`'s measurement argument is in its founding case here. **The English television market's name for it is anime-derived and is not this work's title.**

entries.category: SF, Mecha and the Speculative Line
entries.name: サイボーグ009 / Cyborg 009
entries.author: Ishinomori Shōtarō
entries.description: Monthly serial. Nine people rebuilt as weapons and then refusing the war they were built for, serialised subsequently across many magazines — **a…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Nine people rebuilt as weapons and then refusing the war they were built for, serialised subsequently across many magazines — **a single work with no single venue**, which is why a naive venue field would misdescribe it. It discharges a Superhero debt subject, and the delta this pack reads is the serialisation history rather than the team structure: a work that outlived several of its magazines is a work whose shape was set by that survival.

entries.category: SF, Mecha and the Speculative Line
entries.name: マジンガーZ / Mazinger Z
entries.author: Nagai Gō
entries.description: Weekly serial. The piloted giant robot — the pilot inside rather than outside, which is the second half of the proposition `work-116` states. Manga…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The piloted giant robot — the pilot inside rather than outside, which is the second half of the proposition `work-116` states. Manga and anime ran simultaneously and only the manga is carded, per the pack's boundary rule. `author-96` cards the creator who invented three formats in five years and drew a censorship campaign with a fourth.

entries.category: SF, Mecha and the Speculative Line
entries.name: キューティーハニー / Cutie Honey
entries.author: Nagai Gō and Dynamic Pro
entries.description: Weekly serial. A transforming android heroine, and **a media-mix project from the outset**: the manga preceded the October 1973 anime and the two…
entries.text: Weekly serial. A transforming android heroine, and **a media-mix project from the outset**: the manga preceded the October 1973 anime and the two were planned together, which makes it an early and unusually explicit case of `craft-30`'s property-versus-story distinction. It discharges a Superhero debt subject; that pack cards the suffixed manga form and this one cards the bare form, and `debt_work_key()` reconciles them.

entries.category: SF, Mecha and the Speculative Line
entries.name: 風の谷のナウシカ / Kaze no Tani no Nausicaä
entries.author: Miyazaki Hayao
entries.description: Monthly serial. A twelve-year ecological serial drawn intermittently alongside a film career, darker and more politically unresolved than the film…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A twelve-year ecological serial drawn intermittently alongside a film career, darker and more politically unresolved than the film made from its first act — **and the film is not carded**, because they are different objects with different endings. `craft-33`'s adaptation that overtakes the source is this case exactly. The diaeresis in the romanisation is a live variant generator and the roster pins one form.

entries.category: SF, Mecha and the Speculative Line
entries.name: AKIRA
entries.author: Ōtomo Katsuhiro
entries.description: Weekly serial. Psychic children and a destroyed Tokyo, drawn with architectural precision and a fixed camera discipline the medium had largely not…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Psychic children and a destroyed Tokyo, drawn with architectural precision and a fixed camera discipline the medium had largely not bothered with. Its English edition was many readers' first manga, **and early US editions were mirrored to read left to right** — which preserves every panel's content while reversing the clock, the demonstration `page-1` is built on. The printed title is Latin; the creator's name is a macron cluster pass N flagged.

entries.category: SF, Mecha and the Speculative Line
entries.name: 攻殻機動隊 / Kōkaku Kidōtai
entries.author: Shirow Masamune
entries.description: Monthly serial. Cyberpunk with its technical and political apparatus elaborated in marginal notes running alongside the story — text density…
entries.text: Monthly serial. Cyberpunk with its technical and political apparatus elaborated in marginal notes running alongside the story — text density competing with the art deliberately, which is the exact inverse of `craft-27`'s division of labour and is worth studying as the counter-case rather than as a failure. **The cover carries an English title beside the kanji and the two are not translations of each other**, which the roster records as two names for one object rather than a title and its rendering.

entries.category: Comedy, Gag and Yonkoma
entries.name: サザエさん / Sazae-san
entries.author: Hasegawa Machiko
entries.description: Yonkoma strip. The medium's longest-lived strip: an ordinary family, four panels, published from 1946 and moved to a national daily in 1951, with a…
entries.text: Yonkoma strip. The medium's longest-lived strip: an ordinary family, four panels, published from 1946 and moved to a national daily in 1951, with a television adaptation running continuously since 1969. The four-panel unit is used with complete discipline — setup, development, turn, conclusion, nothing overspilling — which `subgenre-2` argues is structural rather than a gag format that happens to have four panels, and `page-14` cites as the grid that makes a single departure legible.

entries.category: Comedy, Gag and Yonkoma
entries.name: 天才バカボン / Tensai Bakabon
entries.author: Akatsuka Fujio
entries.description: Weekly serial. Gag manga built on absurdity with internal consistency — the rules are insane and they are rules — and a cast designed as pure…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Gag manga built on absurdity with internal consistency — the rules are insane and they are rules — and a cast designed as pure recognisable shapes that outlived their strips into common speech. **Some of the material makes jokes on disability and on class that read differently now**, and the card states that rather than passing over it: `checklist-14` applies, and the register is period-specific in a way a writer borrowing the structure should notice before borrowing the jokes.

entries.category: Comedy, Gag and Yonkoma
entries.name: ドラえもん / Doraemon
entries.author: Fujiko F. Fujio
entries.description: Monthly serial. A children's science-fiction serial with a fixed engine — a problem, a gadget, a misuse, a consequence — repeated for thousands of…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A children's science-fiction serial with a fixed engine — a problem, a gadget, a misuse, a consequence — repeated for thousands of instalments without exhausting itself, and drawn for readers learning to read. `page-26` is best studied here, because a children's page has no tolerance for ambiguous balloon order. **The byline at first appearance was the two-person pen name and was resplit in 1987**, which is the joint-byline case `serial-57` cards and `author-61` and `author-62` carry from both sides.

entries.category: Comedy, Gag and Yonkoma
entries.name: こちら葛飾区亀有公園前派出所 / Kochira Katsushika-ku Kameari Kōen-mae Hashutsujo
entries.author: Akimoto Osamu
entries.description: Weekly serial. Forty years of weekly comedy in the same magazine with the same cast — the longest continuous run in that magazine's history, ended…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Forty years of weekly comedy in the same magazine with the same cast — the longest continuous run in that magazine's history, ended on the creator's decision rather than on a survey. The structure is the only one that survives that many instalments: a fixed premise refreshed by subject matter rather than by escalation. `psychology-10`'s duration argument has no better case. **It is universally abbreviated**, and the roster carries the full title because the abbreviation is not the name.

entries.category: Comedy, Gag and Yonkoma
entries.name: あずまんが大王 / Azumanga Daiō
entries.author: Azuma Kiyohiko
entries.description: Monthly serial. A four-panel school serial with no plot and no antagonist, in a seinen-market monthly, which established the low-stakes ensemble…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A four-panel school serial with no plot and no antagonist, in a seinen-market monthly, which established the low-stakes ensemble comedy as a commercial category. The timing is built on the absence of event — the humour is reaction to nothing much — and `subgenre-21`'s nichijō-kei register is largely this work's inheritance. Note the venue: a yonkoma about schoolgirls in an adult men's monthly is `checklist-8`'s demographic point in one line.

entries.category: Historical, Jidaigeki and the War Record
entries.name: はだしのゲン / Hadashi no Gen
entries.author: Nakazawa Keiji
entries.description: Weekly serial. An autobiographical account of Hiroshima and after, serialised in a boys' weekly, and the medium's most widely read work of war…
entries.text: Weekly serial. An autobiographical account of Hiroshima and after, serialised in a boys' weekly, and the medium's most widely read work of war testimony. **It has been the subject of repeated Japanese school-library access disputes**, from Matsue in 2012–13 onward, in which restriction and restoration have both been argued on educational grounds — and both positions are on the record. This pack states the disputes and adjudicates none of them. `trope-68`'s survivor's account and `checklist-14` are the instruments.

entries.category: Historical, Jidaigeki and the War Record
entries.name: 総員玉砕せよ! / Sōin Gyokusai Seyo!
entries.author: Mizuki Shigeru
entries.description: Volume-first work. The author's own Rabaul service, drawn as a single volume rather than serialised — which is why it has no magazine — depicting an…
entries.text: Volume-first work. The author's own Rabaul service, drawn as a single volume rather than serialised — which is why it has no magazine — depicting an ordered mass death of Japanese troops. **It contradicts the account the survivors were given** and names the command decisions, and it was produced over decades against a market that preferred his folklore work. `author-91` cards the creator; `history-12` cards the period. Testimony, stated as testimony.

entries.category: Historical, Jidaigeki and the War Record
entries.name: 無限の住人 / Mugen no Jūnin
entries.author: Samura Hiroaki
entries.description: Monthly serial. A cursed immortal swordsman across a long historical serial, drawn with an unusually loose, sketch-like line for the genre and with…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A cursed immortal swordsman across a long historical serial, drawn with an unusually loose, sketch-like line for the genre and with violence that refuses to be clean. Its formal interest is the fight staged as bad geometry — bodies in the wrong positions, weapons that are difficult to read — which is a deliberate inversion of `superhero:craft-9`'s legibility rule rather than a failure of it.

entries.category: Historical, Jidaigeki and the War Record
entries.name: バガボンド / Vagabond
entries.author: Inoue Takehiko
entries.description: Weekly serial. Miyamoto Musashi adapted from Yoshikawa Eiji's novel, drawn substantially in brush, and **on hiatus since 2015** — a live…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Miyamoto Musashi adapted from Yoshikawa Eiji's novel, drawn substantially in brush, and **on hiatus since 2015** — a live incompletion rather than a finished work, and the second such case in the collection. `page-12` cites its alternation of dense small-panel sequences with pages given to one image; the contrast rather than either register is what sets the book's rhythm.

entries.category: Historical, Jidaigeki and the War Record
entries.name: 新・ゴーマニズム宣言SPECIAL 戦争論 / Shin Gōmanizumu Sengen SPECIAL: Sensōron
entries.author: Kobayashi Yoshinori
entries.description: Volume-first work. A polemical revisionist account of the Asia-Pacific War in comics form, which sold in very large numbers and was argued about…
entries.text: Volume-first work. A polemical revisionist account of the Asia-Pacific War in comics form, which sold in very large numbers and was argued about nationally. **Both positions are on the record and both are serious**: it was supported in parts of the Japanese conservative press as a corrective to what its supporters regard as a one-sided postwar account, and criticised by historians as revisionism that misstates the record. **This pack states the dispute and does not adjudicate it**, and cards the work because a collection describing the medium's engagement with the war that omitted its most commercially successful revisionist argument would be describing a different medium. `checklist-13` and `history-11` are the neighbouring instruments.

entries.category: Historical, Jidaigeki and the War Record
entries.name: ヴィンランド・サガ / Vinland Saga
entries.author: Yukimura Makoto
entries.description: Weekly serial. Vikings, vengeance and a long argument against both, begun in a boys' weekly and moved to a monthly. **The transfer is documented as…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Vikings, vengeance and a long argument against both, begun in a boys' weekly and moved to a monthly. **The transfer is documented as a pace failure** — the story the author was telling could not be told at weekly speed — which makes it the cleanest case the Serialisation collection has for `serial-13`'s rhythms being a craft constraint rather than a scheduling detail, and for `craft-53`'s move between magazines as a decision with consequences.

entries.category: Gambling, Mahjong and Competitive Skill
entries.name: 麻雀飛翔伝 哭きの竜 / Mājan Hishōden: Naki no Ryū
entries.author: Nōjō Jun'ichi
entries.description: Anthology serial. A near-silent mahjong player in a specialist gambling magazine, running to 1990 — the medium's demonstration that a game manga can…
entries.text: Anthology serial.
