A near-silent mahjong player in a specialist gambling magazine, running to 1990 — the medium's demonstration that a game manga can work without explaining the game, because the reader is watching the players rather than the tiles. **It is almost always cited by the bare subtitle**, which the roster records; the full title is what is carded.

entries.category: Gambling, Mahjong and Competitive Skill
entries.name: 賭博黙示録カイジ / Tobaku Mokushiroku Kaiji
entries.author: Fukumoto Nobuyuki
entries.description: Weekly serial. Debt, a gambling ship and games with lives attached, in which the rules are explained so completely that the reader can check the…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Debt, a gambling ship and games with lives attached, in which the rules are explained so completely that the reader can check the protagonist's reasoning — which is what makes the tension survive the explanation. **The series changes title with each part**, so one work carries five printed titles; a roster that indexed the current one would lose the work's own history, and `checklist-15` audits exactly this.

entries.category: Gambling, Mahjong and Competitive Skill
entries.name: ヒカルの碁 / Hikaru no Go
entries.author: Hotta Yumi · Obata Takeshi
entries.description: Weekly serial. Competitive go with no violence and no tournament ladder in the battle sense — a serial that ran successfully in a boys' weekly on…
entries.text: Weekly serial. Competitive go with no violence and no tournament ladder in the battle sense — a serial that ran successfully in a boys' weekly on the strength of a game most of its readers could not play. `page-9` cites it as a positive case for reveals sitting on turn positions consistently enough that the layout was clearly planned around pagination. The writer and artist are separately credited, and `author-115` cards the artist who works to other people's scripts by choice.

entries.category: Gourmet, Work and the Everyday
entries.name: 美味しんぼ / Oishinbo
entries.author: Kariya Tetsu · Hanasaki Akira
entries.description: Weekly serial. The long-running gourmet serial that made food a major manga genre, structured as a contest — two dishes, two positions, a verdict —…
entries.text: Weekly serial. The long-running gourmet serial that made food a major manga genre, structured as a contest — two dishes, two positions, a verdict — which turns instruction into drama. **In 2014 instalments depicting nosebleeds attributed to radiation exposure near Fukushima drew objection from national and prefectural government and from parts of the medical community, and the serial was suspended.** Both positions are on the record: that the sequence reported what people at the site told the author, and that a fiction serial making health claims carries an evidential burden it did not meet. `checklist-11` is the instrument; the pack does not settle it.

entries.category: Gourmet, Work and the Everyday
entries.name: 孤独のグルメ / Kodoku no Gurume
entries.author: Kusumi Masayuki · Taniguchi Jirō
entries.description: Monthly serial. A man eats alone, and the serial is about the eating rather than the food's preparation — the register that separates it from the…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A man eats alone, and the serial is about the eating rather than the food's preparation — the register that separates it from the contest structure of `work-137`. Running to 1996 and revived from 2008, it is `trope-64`'s eating alone in its defining case, and the interior monologue does work the dialogue cannot because there is nobody to talk to.

entries.category: Gourmet, Work and the Everyday
entries.name: きのう何食べた? / Kinō Nani Tabeta?
entries.author: Yoshinaga Fumi
entries.description: Monthly serial. A gay couple's domestic life organised around cooking, published in a men's magazine by a creator who came out of the BL circuit —…
entries.text: Monthly serial. A gay couple's domestic life organised around cooking, published in a men's magazine by a creator who came out of the BL circuit — **the demographic-crossing case in one object**: BL-origin creator, seinen venue, domestic subject, and a readership that matches none of the categories cleanly. `checklist-8` and `craft-51` are the instruments, and `author-46` cards the career the crossing belongs to.

entries.category: Gourmet, Work and the Everyday
entries.name: 重版出来! / Jūhan Shuttai!
entries.author: Matsuda Naoko
entries.description: Anthology serial. The manga industry as procedural subject — editors, sales figures, print runs, the decision to reprint — and the pack's most-cited…
entries.text: Anthology serial. The manga industry as procedural subject — editors, sales figures, print runs, the decision to reprint — and the pack's most-cited work in the Serialisation collection for that reason. Its most useful contribution is showing editorial decisions as commercial, unmalicious and not about merit, which is the texture `serial-31` and `serial-54` describe. **The title's 出来 reads *shuttai*, not *deki***, a trap the roster holds.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 未来少年コナン / Mirai Shōnen Conan
entries.author: Miyazaki Hayao
entries.description: Anime television series. **Adapted from an English-language novel with no manga source**, which is why the anime is the primary text rather than an…
entries.text: Anime television series. **Adapted from an English-language novel with no manga source**, which is why the anime is the primary text rather than an adaptation of one — the criterion this whole block turns on. It is also the clearest early demonstration of a director's serial-television grammar: episode-length structure, a fixed cast, and escalation managed across a broadcast run rather than a page count. `craft-31`'s question of what survives the move to motion is not the right question here, because nothing moved.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 機動戦士ガンダム / Kidō Senshi Gundam
entries.author: Tomino Yoshiyuki
entries.description: Anime television series. Anime-original, and the work that separated the piloted robot from the superhero premise: a mass-produced military machine…
entries.text: Anime television series. Anime-original, and the work that separated the piloted robot from the superhero premise: a mass-produced military machine with a supply chain and a chain of command, rather than a hero's body. `work-118`'s pilot-inside proposition is answered here by making the machine ordinary. **The director's given name was printed one way at the time and another later**, which the roster records because a creator who respells is a phantom-duplicate generator.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 超時空要塞マクロス / Chōjikū Yōsai Macross
entries.author: Ishiguro Noboru (chief director) · Kawamori Shōji
entries.description: Anime television series. Anime-original, broadcast from October 1982 to June 1983, and the case where the mecha line acquires the other two elements…
entries.text: Anime television series. Anime-original, broadcast from October 1982 to June 1983, and the case where the mecha line acquires the other two elements it is now inseparable from — a pop-music career and a love triangle carried at the same weight as the war. The craft point is structural: three genres running simultaneously rather than alternating, which a weekly manga's page budget could not have afforded.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン / Shin Seiki Evangelion
entries.author: Anno Hideaki
entries.description: Anime television series. **Anime-original: the manga is the adaptation, not the source**, and gets that backwards in a large share of…
entries.text: Anime television series. **Anime-original: the manga is the adaptation, not the source**, and gets that backwards in a large share of English-language writing. The card exists partly to state the direction of dependence. Its production history — a schedule collapse that became a formal choice — is the clearest case in the block of `serial-31`'s pressure operating in another medium, with the same result: the ending is shaped by what could be finished. The official English title is not a translation of the Japanese and the roster holds both.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 少女革命ウテナ / Shōjo Kakumei Utena
entries.author: Ikuhara Kunihiko
entries.description: Anime television series. **The manga began publishing before the broadcast and is still not the source**: it is credited as a comicalisation of an…
entries.text: Anime television series. **The manga began publishing before the broadcast and is still not the source**: it is credited as a comicalisation of an original by the production group, which makes this the block's most instructive case for what *primary text* means. Earlier publication is not priority. The work itself takes the shōjo transformation vocabulary `page-22` cards and runs it as ritual repetition at a length no magazine would permit.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: カウボーイビバップ / Cowboy Bebop
entries.author: Watanabe Shinichirō
entries.description: Anime television series. Anime-original, and the episodic structure at its most disciplined: near-standalone episodes with a serialised undertow,…
entries.text: Anime television series. Anime-original, and the episodic structure at its most disciplined: near-standalone episodes with a serialised undertow, which is `trope-60`'s client of the week carrying a long arc underneath. It is also the block's clearest case of a work built for an international audience before it had one, and of a soundtrack doing structural work — a resource the page does not have and `page-25`'s line register is the nearest equivalent to.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: serial experiments lain
entries.author: Nakamura Ryūtarō · Konaka Chiaki
entries.description: Anime television series. Anime-original, and formally the strangest work in the block: long silences, static compositions held past comfort, and an…
entries.text: Anime television series. Anime-original, and formally the strangest work in the block: long silences, static compositions held past comfort, and an information structure that withholds rather than reveals. **The title is printed in lower-case Latin with no Japanese 原題 and must not be title-cased**, which the roster pins because normalisation is exactly what a citation pipeline does to it. `page-5`'s deliberate ambiguity is the nearest page-side analogue.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 天元突破グレンラガン / Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann
entries.author: Imaishi Hiroyuki
entries.description: Anime television series. Anime-original, and the mecha line's most explicit argument with itself: escalation taken past the point of physical…
entries.text: Anime television series. Anime-original, and the mecha line's most explicit argument with itself: escalation taken past the point of physical meaning on purpose, with each stage announced. `comedy:timing-28`'s requirement that the axis be chosen in advance is met literally — the axis is scale and the work says so — and `trope-16`'s ladder that runs out is the structure it deliberately runs off the end of.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 火垂るの墓 / Hotaru no Haka
entries.author: Takahata Isao
entries.description: Anime film. Adapted from Nosaka Akiyuki's story, and the block's hardest card. It depicts civilian death in the 1945 firebombing through two…
entries.text: Anime film. Adapted from Nosaka Akiyuki's story, and the block's hardest card. It depicts civilian death in the 1945 firebombing through two children, and **its reception is genuinely divided**: read widely as an anti-war film, and read — including by its own director, who said as much — as something other than that, closer to an argument about the boy's refusal of the community around him. Both readings are on the record and this pack states them and settles neither. `checklist-14` and `history-11` are the neighbouring instruments.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: パーフェクトブルー / Perfect Blue
entries.author: Kon Satoshi
entries.description: Anime film. From Takeuchi Yoshikazu's novel, and built on a formal device the page cannot perform: cuts between a performance, a memory and a…
entries.text: Anime film. From Takeuchi Yoshikazu's novel, and built on a formal device the page cannot perform: cuts between a performance, a memory and a delusion with no marker distinguishing them, so the viewer's uncertainty is produced by editing rather than described. **It depicts the sexual assault and stalking of an idol performer**, which is the film's subject rather than an incident in it, and `checklist-14` applies to any writer drawing on it.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 千と千尋の神隠し / Sen to Chihiro no Kamikakushi
entries.author: Miyazaki Hayao
entries.description: Anime film. Anime-original, and the most widely seen Japanese animated film in the world. Its craft interest for a writer is refusal of explanation:…
entries.text: Anime film. Anime-original, and the most widely seen Japanese animated film in the world. Its craft interest for a writer is refusal of explanation: the spirit world's rules are never systematised, characters act on obligations the audience infers, and the film is legible anyway — the opposite of `trope-19`'s named cost and evidence that the rule-system approach is a choice rather than a requirement. **The English title bears no relation to the Japanese one.**

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 時をかける少女 / Toki o Kakeru Shōjo
entries.author: Hosoda Mamoru
entries.description: Anime film. An adaptation that is neither of the novel nor of the earlier live-action films but a sequel to them, made for an audience that mostly…
entries.text: Anime film. An adaptation that is neither of the novel nor of the earlier live-action films but a sequel to them, made for an audience that mostly did not know that. The time-travel premise is used for an ordinary adolescent problem rather than for spectacle, which is the block's best illustration of a genre device carrying domestic material. **The title collides with a 1965 novel and earlier films outside this roster**, and the pack's §8 rule needs no suffix only because nothing here collides with it.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: この世界の片隅に / Kono Sekai no Katasumi ni
entries.author: Katabuchi Sunao
entries.description: Anime film. Adapted from a manga **that this roster deliberately does not card**, which leaves the bare name free for the film — a disambiguation…
entries.text: Anime film. Adapted from a manga **that this roster deliberately does not card**, which leaves the bare name free for the film — a disambiguation decision made at roster stage rather than discovered at merge. Wartime Kure and the Hiroshima bombing, told through domestic routine at a level of researched material detail that is itself the argument: the war is legible through rationing, cooking and cloth rather than through battle. `checklist-12`'s what-it-looked-like audit has no better case.

entries.category: The Anime as Primary Text
entries.name: 君の名は。 / Kimi no Na wa.
entries.author: Shinkai Makoto
entries.description: Anime film. Anime-original, and the commercial event that made a non-Ghibli anime film a global object. Structurally it is a body-swap comedy that…
entries.text: Anime film. Anime-original, and the commercial event that made a non-Ghibli anime film a global object. Structurally it is a body-swap comedy that turns into a disaster narrative, with the turn placed so that the audience reinterprets everything before it — `page-8`'s withholding across the turn, executed once at feature length. **The trailing 。 is part of the title** and is dropped in most citations, which the roster holds.

entries.category: Criticism, History and the Scholarship
entries.name: Manga! Manga! The World of Japanese Comics
entries.author: Frederik L. Schodt
entries.description: Criticism. The first substantial English-language account of the medium as a medium with a history, and the book most Anglophone readers' idea of…
entries.text: Criticism. The first substantial English-language account of the medium as a medium with a history, and the book most Anglophone readers' idea of manga still descends from. **There is no Japanese 原題** — it is an English-language book, the pack's name-form rule cannot apply, and the printed title is the name. Its shape matters as much as its content: what it chose to cover first set the English record's centre of gravity for decades, which `author-119` cards and `history-12` relies on.

entries.category: Criticism, History and the Scholarship
entries.name: 現代マンガの全体像 / Gendai Manga no Zentaizō
entries.author: Kure Tomofusa
entries.description: Criticism. A Japanese-language survey arguing that the medium's categories are historical products rather than natural kinds — the frame this pack's…
entries.text: Criticism. A Japanese-language survey arguing that the medium's categories are historical products rather than natural kinds — the frame this pack's Subgenre collection and `checklist-8` both work inside. **The author's name is a pen name read *Kure Tomofusa* though the characters also read *Go Chiei***, a live reading trap the roster records, and one this pack's own Creator collection got wrong until screen 33's attribution half was built.

entries.category: Criticism, History and the Scholarship
entries.name: 物語消費論 / Monogatari Shōhiron
entries.author: Ōtsuka Eiji
entries.description: Criticism. The argument that audiences buy fragments of a larger fictional world rather than individual stories, developed from a study of…
entries.text: Criticism. The argument that audiences buy fragments of a larger fictional world rather than individual stories, developed from a study of collectible stickers and subsequently made to look descriptive by the industry's own media-mix. `craft-30`'s property-versus-story distinction is this book's claim in craft form. The author is the four-way romanisation cluster pass N named, and the pack holds one form throughout.

entries.description: Criticism. The multi-author volume that supplied the vocabulary for discussing the manga page as a technical object — panel, frame, line, balloon,…
entries.text: Criticism. The multi-author volume that supplied the vocabulary for discussing the manga page as a technical object — panel, frame, line, balloon, the treatment of the gutter. **The pack's entire Page collection is downstream of this line of criticism**, which is why `page-1` through `page-30` can be written as cards rather than as impressions. The title is generic enough to collide with any how-to book, which the roster flags.

entries.text: Criticism. A sociological study of the commercial industry and the amateur movement and the relationship between them, including editorial control, the 1990–91 regulation campaign, and the periods when the two systems were hostile rather than symbiotic. `serial-63`, `serial-64` and `history-21` all rest on it. **Two 2000 imprints in two territories** will read as two editions or two years to a naive pass, which the roster records.

entries.author: Eike Exner
entries.description: Criticism. The sustained argument against the chōjū-giga origin story and against several priority claims made for Tezuka, holding that modern manga…
entries.text: Criticism. The sustained argument against the chōjū-giga origin story and against several priority claims made for Tezuka, holding that modern manga assembles in the twentieth century out of imported newspaper-strip conventions. **The pack carries it as one side of a live dispute and not as the settled account**: `history-1`, `history-3` and `history-4` state the argument, and `author-118` cards the historian whose primary-source work runs the other way. Blueprint §9 requires both, and a collection that carded only this book would have adjudicated the question it says it does not adjudicate.
